I just took a trip to China. A lot of players go over for a brand tour. Press run, appearances, flight home. This go around, my team and I wanted to do it differently: go see the country for real, meet the fans, and start my relationship with that part of the world authentically. The branded trips have their place, and those will come too. This one was about something else. I stood on the Great Wall early in the morning before the heat rolled in. Ate Peking duck in Beijing. And in Hong Kong I got to the Bruce Lee landmark, which was incredible. You can't stand in front of Bruce Lee and not lock back in. That man was discipline. Made me want to get straight back to the gym. And I did. Got plenty of work in the whole trip. Wherever I was, I found a way to train. That part doesn't stop, ever, just because the scenery changes. I didn't know what to expect going into the trip. What I found was warmth. Fans who waited hours to say hi. Kids who knew my BYU stats. People treated me like they'd known me for years. France taught me this summer that my world is bigger than I thought. China confirmed it. Basketball fans are everywhere, and I plan to show up for them. I'll be back. That's a promise. ...more ...more

Excited to share that I've officially completed my first week as a Forward Deployment Engineer Intern at Five9! This week has been an incredible introduction to what it means to work on real production software. I've been working alongside Kevin Kochpatcharin and under the guidance of Ravi Kanagala on Five9's Automated Quality Management (AQM) system — an AI-powered platform that uses large language models to automatically score call center interactions and evaluate agent performance at scale. In just my first week I've been diving deep into the codebase, setting up my local development environment, running data sampling scripts against live BigQuery datasets, and getting hands-on experience onboarding new enterprise clients onto the AQM platform. It's been incredibly rewarding to be contributing to a product that real customers are actively using. What's made this experience even better is going through it alongside an amazing intern cohort — it's been great having people to learn and grow with from day one. So grateful for the opportunity to be doing meaningful work from week one. Can't wait to see what the rest of the summer brings! #Five9 #ForwardDeployment #SoftwareEngineering #Internship #AI #MachineLearning #CloudComputing ...more ...more

My time in Madison has ended much sooner than I expected. This fall, I’ll be transferring from the University of Wisconsin–Madison to Vanderbilt University, where I plan to study Computer Science and Mathematics. In just one year, Madison gave me more than I could have asked for: professors who stayed after class until every question was answered, mentors that took 2am calls, friends who made Madison feel like home, and the opportunity to contribute to UW’s growing entrepreneurship community. Leaving those people and opportunities behind has made this an incredibly difficult decision. Ultimately, I realized that I wanted to take the risk of starting over and place myself in a new environment that would challenge me both academically and personally. At Vanderbilt, I’m looking forward to going deeper into math and computer science, continuing my work in machine learning through pyrent.ai , and meeting a new community of students and professors in Nashville. I’m especially grateful to Lewis Sheats , Maia Patrick Donohue , and Jon Eckhardt for the mentorship and many opportunities you’ve created for me and other student founders at UW. Thanks to Ben Lukszys , Tarun Vedula , and Siddharth Singh for the candid conversations and continued support. And thank you to professors An Panduan and Jeremy Beach for advocating for me throughout my transfer journey. Huge thanks to everyone else at UW–Madison who made this past year so meaningful. I’m carrying a lot from Madison with me into this next chapter. See you in Nashville! ...more ...more

We built a Turing test that runs backwards. And watching people fail it was the best part. At the Tavus X Lovable hackathon this weekend, we flipped the premise: instead of an AI trying to convince you it's human, you have to convince an AI that you're a machine. You join a video call with a cold AI border agent guarding the "Machine World." To get in, you have to pass as an AI. It interrogates you for 60 seconds and it's brutal, because being human leaks out of you in ways you can't control: cadence, composure, diction and embodiment. Under the hood, the agent runs on Tavus - Phoenix-4 for the face, Raven for real-time perception. We wired custom tool calls so the instant it catches a tell, a structured event fires into our app, which holds the score and drives a live "Humanity Leak" meter. Try it out: https://lnkd.in/dAX9iG5w We flip the polarity here, it becomes a deepfake detector: you can catch AI pretending to be human. Synthetic candidates are already deepfaking their way through remote job interviews. Injected video is bypassing KYC checks in fintech and crypto onboarding. Shoutout to my teammate Alvin A. - none of this would've happened without him 🙌 . Also had a chat with Gagan Bhat from Anthropic on RL environments for AI agents and Claude. Thank you Joshua Bailey Rohan Suggala for hosting such an amazing event! 👏 ...more ...more

I'm in New York City for the NBA Draft. Wild sentence to type. Anyway, you can imagine what it looks like. Gym time. Business meetings. And yesterday, pulled up to LinkedIn 's offices in the Empire State Building. Cool to meet the people behind the platform. And cool to learn from them. How it works, what it's built for, and why it matters for people my age who are just getting into business. For someone coming up, LinkedIn is easy to overlook. It's not where you think the culture lives. But the business is here. The decision-makers are here. Brands look here before they ever DM or email you. That's a first impression you're either building or leaving blank. I'd rather build it up tall like, well, the Empire State Building. Appreciate the hospitality from some of the good folks at LinkedIn. You know who you are. ...more ...more

Number one. The Wizards called my name. All those years of work. All those days of anticipation. It happened just like God planned. Then everything was a blur. Right off the stage, media circuit. Hours of it. Then dinner and a party with the people who've been in my corner for all of this. Somewhere in the middle of the night, drove near Times Square, someone pointed up and I saw my face on a billboard. Big as anything. Just sitting there, static, for the whole NYC to see. Very little sleep after that. Today Show and Good Morning America this morning. Now I'm on my way to DC. We made it to the top. And now I'm starting at the bottom again. First practices. First film sessions. Building with a new team, in a new city, in front of fans I haven't met yet. Earning all of it. There is nowhere I'd rather be starting over. LGI, DC. I'm home. ...more ...more

Typing this in the back of a car rolling through New York City. My dad right next to me. On the way to a workout. Father's Day. The draft is in two days. This man. My dad's got no filter at all. He'll tell you the truth. That's just him. When I told him I wanted the NBA, he said he'd do whatever he could to help me get there. He told me the road would be hard. I said: "Let's do it." Growing up, if an outsider wanted to talk to me, I had one answer: talk to my dad. I trusted him more than anyone in any room. Still do. He was right about that road. And he's done “whatever,” just like he said he would back then. That convo happened years ago. Now, we’re on the verge of making my dream come true. It doesn’t happen without him. Happy Father's Day! ...more ...more

I won the Stanford University x Red Bull x Google GDG Hackathon as a solo founder after pitching live to 20 VCs as well as engineers from OpenAI, Google Deepmind, Microsoft, and Snowflake. Winning earned me meetings with funds writing $500k-$5M seed checks. China turned selling through live streams into a $500B+ market that converts 10x better than normal ecommerce. The US is barely $68B because it still runs on human hosts. These hosts cost around $12,000 a month, sleep 8 hours a day, and speak a single language. LiveGen closes that gap. It's a 24/7 multilingual 3D Al avatar that sells any product live, in any language, for around 99x less than a human. Immensely grateful for the opportunity after getting in on a cold DM and huge thanks to Daniel Goncharov , the Red Bull team, and Stanford University for hosting such a well run event. If you're building in SF this summer I’d love to connect ...more ...more
